problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{5x+8}{(x+2)^{2}}=\frac{5}{x+2}+\frac{B}{(x+2)^{2}},
$$

what is the value of $B?$
worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+2)^{2}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+8 & =5(x+2)+B.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=-2$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5(-2)+8 & =5(-2+2)+B \\ -2 & =0+B \\ B & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
